C347.label: Guernsey · 1893 · 8 Doubles
C347.notes: Both sides photographed in the holder. Reverse: a big 8 over DOUBLES over the date 1893, all inside a laurel wreath with a beaded border — read plainly in an enhanced view (1-8-9-3 certain). Obverse: the Guernsey shield with three lions, GUERNSEY arcing above, very worn with light corrosion patches. Guernsey is the only issuer of doubles coinage, and the 8 doubles of 1885-1911 is the only issue matching this size, wreath reverse and shield obverse; Jersey, the other Channel Island, coined in shillings and pence instead. The mint-mark spot below the date is too dark in these photos to read, so no variety is claimed. Face value note: 8 doubles made one penny, 240 pennies one pound, so the face is recorded as 1/240 of a Guernsey pound.
C347.mint: no mint mark read — the area below the date is too dark in the photos to call
C347.story: Eight doubles from Guernsey, dated 1893 — the oldest coin in this batch, struck while Queen Victoria was on the throne, though Guernsey's coins show no portrait: just the island's shield with its three lions, inherited from the island's Norman past, and a sprig of leaves. The double was Guernsey's own money, a Channel Islands coinage counted eight to a British penny, and this big bronze piece is the penny-sized one — Guernsey kept its doubles for a century before joining the pound in full. It is the collection's first coin from Guernsey. This one has lived a life: dark, worn smooth in places, with pale corrosion spots on the shield side.
